Station 03 · Computer controls

Controls Lab

Recognise the computer, find the key Windows features and choose the correct mouse action.

Key words

Desktop or laptop?

Know your kit

A desktop has separate parts. A laptop combines the computer, screen and keyboard in one portable device.

Both are computersThey run applications, open files and create work.
Controls differA laptop may use a touchpad instead of a mouse.

Four Windows landmarks

Recognise, do not memorise
Windows desktopThe main workspace that appears after you sign in.
Start menuFind applications, settings and power.
TaskbarShows open and pinned applications.
File ExplorerFinds and opens files and folders.

Simplified Windows examples. Your school computer may look a little different; look for the same features.

Match the mouse action

Required

Choose the best action for each task.

1
Select a button once
2
Open a desktop icon
3
See more options for an item
4
Move down a long page
5
Move an item to a new position

Mouse guide

Useful detail: a desktop icon normally opens with a double left-click, but a taskbar icon normally needs only one left-click.

Show me how to explain a choice

Explorer Training · Key terms

Choose a useful word, understand its meaning, then explain how it connects to what you are doing.

Workstation

Is my space ready?

Your computer, equipment and the space around them. A safe workstation protects you and other people.

For example

Keep your bag out of the walkway and report damaged equipment to the teacher.

Account

Who is signed in?

Your identity on a digital system. Your school account gives you access to your own work and classes.

For example

Check that your school name appears before you begin. Keep your password private.

Windows desktop

Where do I start after signing in?

The main Windows workspace. It can show shortcuts, open windows and the taskbar.

For example

After signing in, use the desktop or Start menu to open an application.

Start menu

Where can I find an application?

The Windows menu for finding applications, searching and accessing settings or power options.

For example

Open Start to find an application that is not pinned to the taskbar.

Taskbar

Which applications are available or open?

The strip, usually at the bottom of Windows, containing Start and open or pinned applications.

For example

Select an open browser on the taskbar to return to your workbook.

File Explorer

How do I find a file or folder?

The Windows application for viewing, opening and organising files and folders.

For example

Use File Explorer to find your downloaded picture and check its filename.

Responsible

What does my choice protect?

Make choices that protect people, equipment, learning and accounts. Explain the effect of the action.

For example

Report a loose cable rather than trying to repair it yourself.

Source

Where did this image come from?

The website or creator an image comes from. A search tool can point to a source without being the original source.

For example

Choose a picture from the approved source your teacher has shown you.

Download

Which way does the file travel?

Bring a copy of an online file into your computer or chosen storage location.

For example

Download a picture, find the saved file, then add that copy to this workbook.

Filename

Will I recognise this file later?

The name used to identify a file. A useful name describes its contents; the extension identifies its file type.

For example

mountain-lake.jpg is easier to recognise than image123.jpg. Keep the .jpg ending.

Screenshot

What was visible on the screen?

An image of all or part of a computer screen at a particular moment. Choose only the area needed.

For example

Capture the school homepage, without including private messages or account information.

Clipboard

Where does copied content wait?

Temporary storage for text or images you have copied or cut, ready to paste somewhere else.

For example

After copying a sentence, Ctrl + V pastes the clipboard contents into the answer box.

Shortcut

Can the keyboard carry out this action?

A key or combination of keys that performs an action without using the menus.

For example

Ctrl + C copies selected content. Ctrl + V pastes it.

Upload

How does my saved file reach an online service?

Send a file from your computer into an online service. Uploading a file and submitting an assignment are separate steps.

For example

In Classroom, add the newest saved HTML file to the assignment.

Turn in

Have I submitted the attached work?

Submit an assignment to your teacher after checking that the right work is attached and ready.

For example

Check the filename in Classroom, then select Turn in.

Sign out

Is my account session finished?

End your account session so the next person cannot access your work or use the system as you.

For example

Save your work, sign out, then leave the workstation tidy.

Save

How do I keep my changes?

Create or update a file in a chosen location. In this workbook, Save workbook downloads a new copy containing your latest answers.

For example

After adding your goal, save again so the new copy contains that goal.

Independent

What can I do for myself?

Use what you know and the available instructions to make progress. Asking a useful question can be part of working independently.

For example

Try the shown route, then explain the exact step you need help with.
